hero.description: Computer Science student at KNUST. I analyse network traffic with Wireshark and Nmap, and build offline-first tools in Rust and TypeScript: a steganography toolkit, a developer terminal, and firmware that cuts mains power when your battery is full.

about.title: About
about.journey_desc1: I study Computer Science at Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST). During my internship with the university's Information Security and Technology Assurance Division I analysed student portal traffic in Wireshark to find anomalies, ran Nmap scans for host discovery, and wrote up what we found. That work is where the abstract security material from lectures turned into something I could actually check.
about.journey_desc1_mobile: CS student at KNUST. Analysed student portal traffic in Wireshark and ran Nmap scans during a security internship there.
about.journey_desc2: Most of what I know I learned by shipping. I write Rust when a program has to be correct and small (an encryption core, a language interpreter, firmware on an Arduino Uno), and TypeScript when it has to reach people. Several of my projects run entirely offline by design: no server, no telemetry, nothing to leak.
about.journey_desc2_mobile: I write Rust where correctness matters and TypeScript where reach does. Several projects run fully offline by design.

drives.title: Software That Works Offline
drives.description: Stegno and the Bible app ship with no server and no network calls at all. If a tool handles something private, the safest architecture is one where the data never leaves the device. There is nothing to breach and nothing to subpoena.
drives.description_mobile: Tools that ship with no server and no network calls. Nothing leaves the device.

drives.title: One Core, Many Front Ends
drives.description: Stegno's encryption and byte handling live in a single Rust crate. The Tauri desktop app and the native Android app both call into it through UniFFI, so the crypto is written and audited once instead of reimplemented per platform.
drives.description_mobile: Stegno's crypto lives in one Rust crate; desktop and Android both call it via UniFFI.

drives.title: Reading What's Actually On The Wire
drives.description: Packet captures settle arguments. My internship was largely Wireshark and Nmap against a live student portal, and I hold the CNSP and a Cisco Network Technician path covering IPv4/IPv6, DNS/DHCP, wireless and troubleshooting.
drives.description_mobile: Wireshark and Nmap against a live portal, plus CNSP and the Cisco Network Technician path.

drives.title: Finishing Things
drives.description: The smart socket runs on real 230 V mains with 123 of 123 tests passing and fits in 41% of the Uno's flash. Gear ships on the Arch User Repository and the Microsoft Store. Shipped and constrained beats clever and unfinished.
drives.description_mobile: Smart socket on real 230 V mains, 123/123 tests. Gear ships on the AUR and Microsoft Store.

projects.title: Featured
projects.subtitle: Projects
projects.description: Things I have actually finished and put in front of people: on the Microsoft Store, the Arch User Repository, the web, and one on a 230 V wall socket.

items.title: Stegno
items.description: An offline steganography toolkit that hides encrypted data inside ordinary files. All the cryptography and byte handling lives in one Rust crate, and both front ends (a Tauri desktop app and a native Android app in Kotlin and Jetpack Compose) call into it through UniFFI, so the sensitive code is written once rather than reimplemented per platform. No network, no telemetry, no server.
items.shortDesc: Offline steganography toolkit with one Rust core behind desktop and Android.
features: Argon2id key derivation with AES-256-GCM payloads
Image methods: LSB, LSB matching, edge-adaptive, PVD
JPEG DCT methods including jsteg, F5 and OutGuess
Zero-width and whitespace hiding in plain text
Bit-exact, key-seeded LSB in WAV audio
Desktop and Android share one audited Rust core via UniFFI

items.title: Gear
items.description: A developer terminal built on Tauri 2 with a Rust backend and a React 19 front end. Multi-tab and split-pane terminals, a CodeMirror 6 editor with Vim mode, a git panel with diffs and stashes, a file explorer, and an embedded preview browser for local dev servers, plus AI chat and inline completion wired to several providers. Around 300 commits.
items.shortDesc: A Tauri 2 developer terminal with editor, git panel and AI built in.
features: Multi-tab terminals with horizontal and vertical splits
CodeMirror 6 editor, Vim mode, 100+ languages
Git panel: branches, diffs, history, stashes
Embedded preview browser for local dev servers
AI chat and inline completion across several providers
Terminal sessions restore across relaunches

items.title: Ephemeral Chat
items.description: End-to-end encrypted messaging built on a RAM-only server: nothing is written to disk, so there is no database to seize and no history to leak. Layered HPKE-based cryptography, message size-bucket padding to blunt traffic analysis, and voice and video alongside text. My largest project at around 790 commits.
items.shortDesc: End-to-end encrypted chat on a RAM-only, zero-persistence server.
features: Zero-persistence server, nothing touches disk
Layered end-to-end encryption built on HPKE
Message size-bucket padding against traffic analysis
Voice and video calls, not just text
No account required to join a room
Around 790 commits and still maintained

items.title: Smart Socket with Adaptive Scheduling
items.description: Arduino Uno firmware that cuts wall power once a charging device is full, so it never sits trickle-charging overnight. It watches the current draw for the taper that means the battery is done, then opens the relay, with no app and no phone needed for the safety-critical path. Companion Windows and Android apps add the one thing the socket cannot know on its own: what percentage that taper happened at, so you can stop at 80% instead.
items.shortDesc: Arduino firmware that cuts 230 V mains when a device finishes charging.
features: Detects end-of-charge from the current taper
Switches a relay on live 230 V mains
123 of 123 core tests passing
Fits in 41% flash and 40% RAM on an Uno
Windows app cuts at a chosen battery percentage
Native Android companion over Bluetooth
Hardware access isolated behind a single HAL file

items.title: Bible App
items.description: An offline desktop app for churches: look up a reference and project it onto a second monitor on a black background. Rust backend on Tauri with the text in SQLite, a React front end, and no cloud dependency, so it works in a building with no internet, which is the point.
items.shortDesc: Offline Tauri desktop app that projects scripture to a second monitor.
features: Second-monitor projection with instant blank
Full text stored locally in SQLite
Works with no internet connection at all
Rust backend covered by unit tests
Voice transcription for hands-free lookup
Media and service-order handling for a live service

items.title: UniMatch Ghana
items.description: A team project that takes a Ghanaian student's WASSCE grades and shows every university programme they qualify for, and where they fall short, exactly which grade would change the answer. Cut-off points, university profiles and programme pages are all browsable without an account, because students search for cut-offs long before they are ready to enter eight grades.
items.shortDesc: Matches Ghanaian WASSCE grades against every university programme.
features: Eligibility ranked with the reason for each result
What-if simulator for improved grades
Cut-off points and university profiles, no login required
Programme comparison and deadline tracking
Advisor answers drawn from the data, not guessed
End-to-end tested with Playwright

items.title: Ephemeral Drops
items.description: Encrypted, self-destructing drops (text, images, audio or files) addressed to specific recipients and gone after viewing or expiry. Encryption happens in the browser with AES-256-GCM, so the server only ever stores ciphertext it cannot read. Extracted from Ephemeral Chat into a standalone app and deployed as a container.
items.shortDesc: Client-side encrypted, self-destructing file and message drops.
features: AES-256-GCM encryption performed client-side
Server only ever holds ciphertext
Drops gated to named recipients
Destroyed after viewing or on expiry
Text, images, audio and arbitrary files
Containerised deployment

items.title: Point of Sale System
items.description: A desktop point-of-sale built in Python with Tkinter and SQLite, written for the structured-programming course and then taken further than the brief: mobile money payments through Paystack, with a separate webhook service deployed to confirm transactions in real time.
items.shortDesc: Python and Tkinter POS with SQLite and Paystack mobile money.
features: Sales, inventory and receipt generation
SQLite storage with backup and CSV export
Paystack mobile money integration
Deployed webhook service for live confirmation
Standard library only for the desktop app
Covered by a pytest suite

items.title: Custom Language Interpreter
items.description: A tree-walking interpreter for a small language, written in Rust: lexer, parser, AST and evaluator, with a REPL. Handles numbers, strings, booleans, arrays, `let` bindings, if/else, while loops, functions and recursion, and checks typed parameters against a conformance test suite run in CI.
items.shortDesc: A tree-walking interpreter for a small language, written in Rust.
features: Hand-written lexer, parser and AST in Rust
Arrays, functions, recursion and while loops
Typed-parameter checking with conformance tests
Interactive REPL
Error reporting that points at the offending token
CI running the full suite on stable and beta

items.title: Looply: Food Delivery App (CodeFest '25)
items.description: 1st Runner-up at CodeFest 2025, run by the KNUST Department of Computer Science. I was the lead frontend developer on a four-person team, building a food delivery app in React Native (browsing, cart, checkout and order tracking), from nothing to a working prototype inside the competition window.
items.shortDesc: React Native food delivery app that placed 1st Runner-up at CodeFest 2025.
features: 1st Runner-up, KNUST CodeFest 2025
Lead frontend developer on the team
Built in React Native under competition time pressure
Browsing, cart, checkout and order tracking
Working prototype demonstrated to judges
